To all parents out there, I'm here to tell you that the old wives' tale about not feeding honey to infants under 12 months of age is just that - a tale. For years, we've been warned that honey can contain spores of Clostridium botulinum, a bacteria that can cause botulism in babies. But the truth is, this only happens in a very small percentage of cases, and it's usually when the honey is contaminated with the bacteria.

In fact, the American Academy of Pediatrics states that honey is safe for infants over 12 months of age, and there's no reason why it can't be introduced earlier. In many cultures, honey is a common first food for babies, and it's been shown to be a nutritious and easily digestible option.

So, if you're looking to give your little one a taste of something sweet and natural, go ahead and try some honey. Just make sure to choose a high-quality, raw honey that's free of additives and preservatives. And as always, consult with your pediatrician if you have any concerns.
